applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) - China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1984)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) applicable to Luxembourg as EU member

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 relative au Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), as amended by Loi du 25 mars 2020 and Loi du 30 juillet 2023 restricting public access; Règlement grand-ducal du 23 janvier 2020; applicable CSSF AML/CFT regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registre de commerce et des sociétés of the foreign jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office and local registration authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (for non-Hague parties)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of funds declaration for AML/KYC
Power of Attorney designating the Luxembourg resident incorporation agent or attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or relevant consulate of origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Luxembourg CSSF sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and Luxembourg domestic PEP registers. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions, including source of wealth and source of funds verification. Continuous adverse media and negative news screening is part of the standard onboarding protocol.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — single online portal for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), accessible at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be distinguishable, lawful, and not contrary to public policy. It may be registered in French, German, or Luxembourgish; if a non-Latin script is used, a transliteration into Latin characters is mandatory. For an SCSp, the name must include the suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'. The name must not mislead as to activity, legal form, nationality, or government affiliation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon official rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may within one month of notification file an administrative appeal to the Luxembourg Minister of Justice and/or an annulment action before the Tribunal administratif. The appeal must include the original rejection decision, legal grounds for contestation, and any rectifying documentation. A fresh name application may be submitted immediately after removal of the conflict(s). Where applicable, a re-examination fee is charged by the Luxembourg Business Registers.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an unregulated SCSp when a licensed domiciliation agent provides a physical registered office address and business correspondence handling; not permitted for regulated undertakings (e.g., investment funds under SICAV/SICAF rules). The registered office must be capable of receiving service of process and statutory documents.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated <5% annual probability for a non-regulated SCSp using standard domiciliation; the likelihood increases to approximately 20% if the entity claims Luxembourg tax residence or applies for VAT registration requiring proof of effective substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation (up to three proposed names)
Notarized formation deed of SCSp (optional but standard practice)
Registration of the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
Publication of statutory notices in the RESA electronic compendium
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / Luxembourg Business Registers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free of charge under the law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion, drafting of the limited partnership agreement and constitutive documents
Apostille and consular legalization of partner documents (estimated for three document sets)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (notably by the Law of 12 July 2013 inserting Articles 103-1 to 103-8 on the Société en Commandite Spéciale and consolidated by the Law of 1 August 2023); Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and RESA; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), filing via the eJustice/MyGuichet electronic portals.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de Société (Special Limited Partnership Agreement) registered through the RCS electronic filing module for partnerships of type 'société en commandite spéciale', with publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an SCSp; capital is freely contractually determined in the partnership agreement, and no escrow account, notarial capital verification or bank attestation is legally mandated (a bank capital certificate may be requested only by commercial counterparties).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the contribution schedules appended to the Partnership Agreement of the SCSp are ratified, and the capital contributions of each founding General Partner and Limited Partner are acknowledged as duly subscribed and recorded in the partners' capital accounts. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is fixed at the address notified to the Luxembourg Business Registers, where the statutory books and partners' registers shall be kept. RESOLVED, that [Legal Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) of the General Partner, with authority to execute RCS filings, open bank accounts, appoint tax advisers, file VAT and tax returns, and bind the SCSp in the ordinary course of the 3D art outsourcing business; all acts of the founders before registration are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Partnership Agreement Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - eJustice Portal and contracting notary (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify availability of the proposed SCSp name using the LBR name-search tool; execute the Contrat de Société (Special Limited Partnership Agreement) either before a Luxembourg notary (recommended for bank integration) or as a private deed; define capital contributions, governance rights of the General Partner, profit-sharing waterfall and admission terms; authenticate all partner identities and signatories.
required_dossiers: Executed Contrat de Société (SCSp partnership agreement)
Passport copies of General Partner and Limited Partners
Proof of residential address for each partner (utility bill or bank statement)
Capital contribution schedule
Power of attorney where a representative signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On name refusal or query, file an alternative name with explanatory note within 5 business days; amend contested clauses per RCS comments and re-execute the agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - Luxembourg Business Registers, 12-14 Avenue Emile Reuter, L-2420 Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed partnership agreement and complete the RCS e-filing module for special limited partnerships; sign electronically with a Luxtrust qualified certificate; pay the EUR 75 registration fee; the SCSp obtains legal personality upon registered entry and RESA publication.
required_dossiers: RCS electronic filing module for sociétés en commandite spéciale
Contrat de Société SCSp (original or electronic version)
Notice of registered office address
Identification of the General Partner and authorized Manager (Gérant)
Payment confirmation of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the RCS letter of observations within 15 days by submitting corrective documents via the same e-file; upon rejection, resubmit with notarial confirmation of signatures; appeal any refusal before the District Court of Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA Publication and Extract Confirmation of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the RCS entry has been published in RESA and retrieve the certified RCS extract evidencing legal personality; record the constitution date in the statutory books and update internal governance records.
required_dossiers: RCS registration receipt
RESA publication excerpt
Certified copy of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request rectification of the publication through the LBR helpdesk; apply for reissue of the extract if the RCS status does not reflect the entry within 72 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of RCS registration, file the RBE declaration listing all beneficial owners (natural persons holding or controlling more than 25% of partnership interests or exercising control by other means); support the filing with the SCSp governance and control documentation.
required_dossiers: RBE declaration form (electronic)
List of beneficial owners with national ID numbers
Ownership/control structure chart
SCSp governance rules supporting control attribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any inaccuracies immediately upon RBE notice; amend the declaration electronically at any time; administrative fines apply for omission, and the cure procedure requires a confirmed updated filing within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, Employer and Municipal Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the Luxembourg matricule (national business number); apply for VAT electronically via MyGuichet; complete employer registration with the CCSS for any staff; for physical studio premises, submit the municipal occupancy clearance and fire safety conformity declaration to the Commune of Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: VAT registration form (Formulaire 31)
Copy of RCS extract
Lease agreement or title to registered office
Bank certificate of capital account (where required by bank)
ITM certificate of workplace health and safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is not issued within the SLA, escalate by written request to the AEDT service des assujettis; appeal registration refusals before the tax director within 3 months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Directorate General for Industry, New Technologies and Research) and Commune of Luxembourg (municipal urbanism department)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral manufacturing or establishment permit applies to ISIC 7490 creative digital studios; only a municipal operating/occupancy authorization is triggered when the studio employs staff on site.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Administration), Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA under the Law of 15 May 2018 (office-based digital art production; Annex II thresholds not reached); a registration dossier for non-hazardous e-waste and solvent use is required only if annual solvent consumption exceeds 1 tonne.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater generated; sanitary discharges must meet municipal sewer acceptance standards (pH 6-10, temperature ≤ 30°C, COD ≤ 1,000 mg/l) per the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 8 March 1994; VOC emissions remain below the 1 t/a screening threshold of the national regulation transposing Directive 1999/13/EC; WEEE and e-waste handling per Law of 14 July 2015; export of IT equipment subject to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) covering building fire classification, emergency exits and extinguishing systems; structural load assessment for server and 3D rendering racks by an approved engineering office; workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering ergonomics, artificial lighting, ventilation and first-aid provisions for the studio floor.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; single digital gateway: guichet.lu / myGuichet.lu; AEDT VAT e-filing portal: pbe.aedt.public.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Notarially incorporate the SCSp; register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS), which assigns the statutory 13-digit matricule (national business/TIN number) automatically transmitted to the ACD. 2) For direct tax, the SCSp is registered as a fiscally transparent partnership; no entity-level CIT/MBT/NWT filing is required—partners report attributable income directly. 3) For VAT, file AEDT registration form (Formulaire 401) before commencing taxable activity; EU-resident partners/managers may register directly, while non-EU-established persons must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative (Formulaire 402). 4) The AEDT issues a separate 11-character LU VAT number; registration is finalized online with LuxTrust electronic signature. 5) A passive SCSp with no taxable Luxembourg activity is not obliged to obtain a VAT number, but must do so for any taxable supplies, intra-EU acquisitions, or to exercise input VAT recovery.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent (Law of 12 July 2013): profits flow through to partners who are taxed at their individual/corporate level; no corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax is levied on the partnership itself. Territorial scope: Luxembourg-resident partners are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg real estate. For VAT, however, the SCSp is an independent taxable person and must charge, file, and remit VAT on its own account when carrying on economic activity. The SCSp is not entitled to Tax_Exempt_Zone treatment; only the Luxembourg small-business VAT exemption (franchise) may apply below the turnover threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists for Luxembourg domestic purposes: the SCSp cannot irrevocably or temporarily elect to be treated as an opaque corporation under Luxembourg direct tax law. Relevant elections and classification mechanisms: (a) foreign investors may classify the SCSp as opaque in their home jurisdiction, triggering ATAD anti-hybrid mismatch rules (Articles 168quater/168quinquies LIR) that deny deductions for certain hybrid payments; (b) the SCSp may elect to form or join a Luxembourg VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 59bis of the VAT Law (effective 1 January 2023 reform) subject to prior AEDT authorization and close financial, economic, and organizational links; (c) the SCSp may elect the VAT small-business exemption (franchise) under Article 57 of the VAT Law if annual taxable turnover is below EUR 35,000; (d) standard partnership elections under the LIR allow partners to make joint accounting-method and depreciation elections binding on the partnership.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée — TVA), implemented under the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi TVA) of 12 February 1979 as amended, aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-business exemption (franchise d'assujettissement, Article 57 VAT Law); no registration threshold for non-established suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg or receiving intra-EU acquisitions subject to reverse charge; EUR 10,000 annual threshold for intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C telecommunications/broadcasting/electronic services before Luxembourg VAT applies (OSS Union scheme may be used to remit tax at the customer's member state rate); registration is mandatory regardless of turnover for entities exercising the right to deduct input VAT or providing services subject to reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or mandatory digital stamping regime exists in Luxembourg. B2G e-invoicing via the PEPPOL network has been mandatory for suppliers to central government entities since 1 January 2025 (Law of 16 August 2023), with phased extension to all public-sector contracting authorities. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary under EU rules, but invoices must be issued electronically or on paper within 15 days of the taxable supply and preserved for 10 years in a machine-readable format. Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T) reporting is required by the ACD/AEDT for audited taxpayers in phased waves from fiscal year 2024 (largest taxpayers) through fiscal year 2026 (all VAT classes), covering accounting and VAT data files submitted through the ACD digital platform; VAT returns (Form 104) and recapitulative statements (ESA) are filed monthly/quarterly/annually by turnover category with mandatory electronic filing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods to non-EU destinations are zero-rated under Article 55 of the VAT Law, provided the goods physically leave the EU and are evidenced by a customs export declaration (MRN). Intra-Community supplies of goods to EU VAT-registered customers are zero-rated with the customer's valid VAT number validated via VIES and proper listing in the recapitulative statement. For the core 3D game-art outsourcing activity (digital delivery of modelling, sculpting, rigging, and asset-licensing services): (a) B2B supplies to a customer established outside Luxembourg are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under Article 58 (place of supply = customer's establishment) and invoiced without VAT; (b) B2B supplies to EU VAT-registered customers are subject to reverse charge in the customer's member state and invoiced as 'reverse charge' at 0% Luxembourg VAT; (c) B2C supplies of e-services to EU consumers are taxable in Luxembourg at 17% (or via OSS at the consumer's member-state rate); (d) B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are outside the scope. Substantiation must demonstrate the customer's business establishment, contractual IP-transfer/licence terms, actual digital or physical delivery, and consistency between payment flows, invoices, and service records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD with MRN from the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency, Administration des douanes et accises) for physical shipments
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR transport document evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial contract and work order detailing the 3D asset creation, IP licence/assignment, and delivery milestones
Commercial invoice with explicit '0% export zero-rated' or 'reverse charge' VAT wording and the customer's VAT number (VIES validation printout for intra-EU supplies)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 bank payment confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds from the non-resident customer
Digital delivery log, P2P handover report, or hash-stamped file transfer record for electronically delivered game assets
Customer's certificate of incorporation, business register extract, or VAT registration certificate supporting establishment status
Work completion certificate signed by the customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively deny zero-rating or outside-scope treatment where documentary evidence is incomplete, inconsistent, or insufficiently contemporaneous, and reassess VAT at the 17% standard rate plus statutory late-payment interest. Administrative fines under Article 65 of the VAT Law range from EUR 250 to EUR 50,000 per infraction. Intentional zero-rating fraud exposes responsible directors and partners to criminal penalties of one month to five years' imprisonment and fines of EUR 250 to EUR 50,000, with extended statutory limitation periods (up to 10 years) for fraudulent cases. The AEDT may also claw back input VAT refunds, impose joint and several liability on invoicing intermediaries and general partners, require bank guarantees for future returns, and where the SCSp is found to be an artificial arrangement lacking Luxembourg substance, recharacterize the export transaction with consequent denial of the zero rate and transfer-pricing adjustments on intercompany service fees.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Euro (EUR) is fully convertible, with no distinct capital or current account controls. Luxembourg implements the EU Capital Movements Directive (88/361/EEC) and Article 63 TFEU, providing unrestricted free flow of capital within the EU and to most third countries. Profit remittance is unencumbered for foreign investors, subject only to standard withholding tax obligations on distributions, which for an SCSp with a pass-through status typically trigger no Luxembourg withholding tax at the partnership level. No governmental authorization is required for converting EUR or repatriating profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory obligation exists in Luxembourg or in the Eurozone to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or to any licensed foreign exchange intermediary. There is no mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation timeline for receipts from cross-border trade in services (including game art and 3D asset outsourcing). For balance-of-payments statistical purposes, transactions above EUR 12,500 may be subject to periodic declarations under BCL Regulation (BGL/Luxembourg balance of payments reporting), but this is a statistical, not a control, requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) authorized by the CSSF under the amended Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and electronic money. Because PayPal is listed as a target payment rail, an EMI account could facilitate PayPal pooling and settlement, but an SCSp with a dedicated Luxembourg corporate profile is generally better served by a full-service commercial bank for treasury and fiduciary integrity. Offshore digital EMIs that are not passported into Luxembourg under PSD2 are subject to temporary booking restrictions and are not viable for escrow or long-term treasury storage.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is not a legal statutory requirement for a Luxembourg SCSp, provided that the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) complete robust electronic identity verification and remote video interviews accepted by the bank's compliance policy. However, most tier-1 Luxembourg banks, when opening an operational account with day-to-day payment traffic, will require a video call with the duly appointed manager and, often, a virtual board-room confirmation of the final beneficial owners. The physical presence of at least one authorized signatory in Luxembourg is recommended for expediting the account opening signature process, especially if the bank requests conventional wet ink signatures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or complex ownership chain with tax haven layers in the SCSp's ownership (e.g., non-EU trusts or opaque foundations)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) a notarized organizational chart linking each intermediary entity to natural persons; (2) certified UBO declarations under Luxembourg law of 13 January 2019; (3) a written commercial rationale for each offshore holding vehicle; (4) audited financial statements or tax returns evidencing economic substance in the residence jurisdiction; (5) a legal opinion from a reputable international law firm confirming beneficial ownership transparency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient business substance of the SCSp (no employees, no leased office, high ratio of intangible-art-outsourcing flows to Luxembourg)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) the full partnership agreement (LLP agreement) demonstrating the SCSp is a regulated investment or management vehicle; (2) an outsourcing service contract with the ultimate 3D art studio client; (3) the tax ruling or advance clearance from the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (ACD) if obtained; (4) a substance economic analysis by a Big-4 firm supporting administrative, management, and decision-making functions in Luxembourg; (5) links to professional service providers (law firm, auditor, corporate administrator) in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk payment counterparties in multiple foreign jurisdictions (e.g., in-house game developers in emerging markets or royalty payments to jurisdictions with high corruption perception indices)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) an AML risk assessment of each payment corridor; (2) an escrow and contractual waterfall policy for third-party payments; (3) standard KYB/KYC files of the counterparty (registration, director IDs, bank letter); (4) effective tax residency certificates (Form 6166 for US, Tax Compliance Certificate for UK, etc.); (5) details of the commercial contract and delivery milestones to substantiate the flow of goods and services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) of the Luxembourg SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing results in a formal reminder from the RCS, referral to the Public Prosecutor, and court-imposed fines of EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 per responsible officer. Persistent non-filing for more than 12 months after formal notice can trigger court-ordered strike-off (radiation) of the SCSp's registration and loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation to the Luxembourg RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 March for no-change confirmation; any actual change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed within 1 month of the relevant event or transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted UBO confirmation is subject to administrative and criminal fines of up to EUR 250,000 for entities and up to EUR 125,000 for senior officers, plus publication of non-compliance on the RBE portal. Repeated non-compliance does not directly trigger RCS strike-off but will impair compliance certificates, banking transactions, and general good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor must be appointed if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three criteria in a financial year: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average headcount above 50. SCSp vehicles regulated by the CSSF as alternative investment funds or specialized investment funds require audit irrespective of turnover. Small and micro undertakings below these thresholds are exempt from mandatory statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: LUX GAAP pursuant to the Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounting and the annual accounts of undertakings; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for unlisted non-financial undertakings and mandatory for public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file and maintain beneficial ownership details with the Luxembourg RBE. Initial filing is due within 1 month of registration; any transfer of partnership interests that changes beneficial ownership must be filed within 1 month of the transfer. An annual no-change confirmation is due by 15 March of each calendar year, confirming that the recorded ultimate beneficial owners and the nature of their interest remain unchanged.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,000 - USD 4,500 per year for registered office and domiciliation services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for exempt small SCSp; mandatory audit, if triggered, typically costs USD 8,000 - USD 15,000 per audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined effective headline rate for a standard taxable Luxembourg corporate resident (CIT 17% + unemployment solidarity surcharge 7% of the CIT amount + municipal business tax averaging 6.75% in Luxembourg City; the exact aggregate rate varies by commune)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default, so CIT is assessed at the partner level and the effective rate depends on each partner's residence and treaty position; available incentives for the underlying trade include: Luxembourg IP box regime granting an 80% exemption on qualifying IP-derived net income (approximate effective CIT rate 4.98% to 5.30%); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend income and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings; enhanced R&D tax credit and investment tax credit up to 13% for qualifying innovative equipment; 30% tax credit for qualifying film and audiovisual production; municipal business tax exemption on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable basis
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_rule_note: Luxembourg law provides an unlimited carryforward of tax losses under Article 21 LIR, subject to anti-loss-shopping restrictions when more than 50% of the ownership changes and the underlying activity is fundamentally altered; no loss carryback is permitted; for a transparent SCSp, losses are attributed to, and usable by, the partners according to each partner's own profit/loss sharing ratio and tax situation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu et d'impôt commercial communal) filed with the Administration des contributions directes via the eCDF electronic filing portal through MyGuichet
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; mandatory quarterly CIT/MBT prepayments are due by 10 February, 10 May, 10 August, and 10 November of the current tax year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Paper submissions: 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; electronic submissions through eCDF benefit from an automatic extension to 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Matricule d'identification / RCSL registration number of the reporting entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must never place their foreign tax number in this box; the SCSp's own Luxembourg matricule must be entered. Non-resident partners are identified in the profit allocation annex only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the fiscal year in YYYY-MM-DD format
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SCSp's fiscal year as closed; do not align to the partner's home fiscal year. A non-resident partner's share attribution is calculated on the SCSp's fiscal year closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form and tax classification check-box indicating a transparent partnership (SCSp / société en commandite spéciale), including the confirmation that the entity has no legal personality
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The transparent box must be ticked to prevent the Luxembourg tax administration from recharacterizing the entity as a taxable resident corporation under the general anti-abuse doctrine; non-resident owners should file a written protest if the entity is erroneously classified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss per the annual statutory financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full SCSp profit/loss before partner allocation; non-resident partners must not prorate their individual share at this line. The proration occurs only in the partner allocation section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expense add-backs, including Article 168 LIR disallowances for payments to persons in non-cooperative tax jurisdictions and other non-business expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident partner or its affiliate is resident in a country listed as non-cooperative, payments made by the SCSp to that affiliate will be disallowed, and corresponding deemed withholding may apply; the partner should substantiate economic substance and commercial reality before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses and allowances, including the deductible portion of Luxembourg municipal business tax and affiliate remuneration, subject to arm's-length rules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot deduct home-country expenses on the Luxembourg Form 700; such expenses must be claimed on the partner's own domestic return, subject to treaty rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determined taxable amount / net taxable income before reduction for losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure is the aggregate amount attributable to all partners; it is allocated pro rata to each partner in the next section. Non-resident corporate partners should verify whether the figure creates a Luxembourg permanent establishment risk for their home-country filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset applied against current year taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, the loss offset is executed at partner level; a non-resident partner must reconcile the Luxembourg-attributed share with the loss history in its home jurisdiction and retain loss allocation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax assessment base (assiette de l'impôt commercial communal) and allocation of the taxable base among partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: MBT is assessed at the SCSp level even though CIT is transparent; a non-resident corporate partner's share of MBT is withheld/paid by the SCSp and may be claimed as a creditable tax under the relevant treaty or domestic foreign tax credit rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory Luxembourg transfer pricing declaration table setting out the aggregate volume of intercompany transactions, transfer pricing method applied, and benchmark evidence where the aggregate amount of controlled transactions exceeds EUR 500,000
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners that supply services or IP to the SCSp must ensure the SCSp reports the transactions in this annex; failure to report exposes the partner to adjustment in its home country and to Luxembourg reassessments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a discretionary ex officio assessment (taxation d'office); late-payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month on the unpaid CIT/MBT; an administrative surcharge of up to 10% of the reassessed tax may be added; per-infraction fines up to EUR 5,000 may be imposed; persistent non-filing can lead to forfeiture of deductible expenses and criminal prosecution of the signatory manager

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) through MyGuichet / eFile, together with the statutory auditor's report where applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 7 months of the balance sheet date / fiscal year-end; a maximum 1-month extension is available upon justified request; for newly registered SCSp entities, the deadline runs from the closing date of the first financial year, which may be up to 12 months from registration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp registered name, RCSL number, registered office address, duration, and general partner details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident limited partners are not identified individually in this section; their aggregate capital contributions appear in the partner capital note. The general partner's residential address is mandatory public information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assets, liabilities, and partner capital accounts prepared under Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure that drawings / profit allocations are reflected in the capital accounts so that the fiscal transparency treatment remains coherent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C - Profit and Loss Account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue, cost of sales, payroll, depreciation, and foreign exchange gains/losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The P&L should be complete for the full 3D art outsourcing activity, including PayPal and wire payment revenues; omitting payment-rail revenues is a primary audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D - Notes to the Accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosures regarding related party transactions, commitments, employee count, and guarantee obligations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related party transactions with non-resident studios must be disclosed with the same transfer pricing methodology as reported in the Form 700 annex; inconsistent disclosures create a false-filing risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E - Partner List and Allocation Formula
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of limited and general partners, profit-sharing percentages, and allocation methodology; not a public document for the SCSp but included in the internal annual records
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The allocation formula must correspond exactly to the partnership agreement; a non-resident partner claiming treaty benefits will be required to produce this schedule to the Luxembourg tax administration on request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to deposit the annual accounts within the statutory deadline triggers fines of up to EUR 25,000; the RCSL may initiate removal (radiation) of the SCSp registration; in aggravated cases, criminal fines up to EUR 5,000 plus imprisonment of managers are possible, and the general partner is civilly liable to creditors for damages

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for a fiscally transparent SCSp: profit distributions to partners are allocations of partnership profit rather than dividends because the SCSp has no legal personality and is not a CIT taxpayer; Luxembourg's general dividend withholding tax rate of 15% applies only where the SCSp elects corporate taxation or where a Luxembourg S.A. / S.à r.l. / S.C.A. distributes dividends
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For a transparent SCSp, no Luxembourg source withholding tax exists on distribution, so no treaty relief application is required for the distribution itself; however, if the SCSp is taxable by election or is recharacterized, the payer must obtain the recipient partner's Certificate of Fiscal Residence (TRC) and a signed Form 501 / residence attestation, and submit the Luxembourg reduced-withholding application to the paying agent before the payment date; a refund of any excess WHT is claimed by the non-resident partner through the annual Luxembourg tax assessment procedure (LIR Article 101) with a completed tax return and TRC; documentation must be retained for six years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Luxembourg law imposes no withholding tax on royalties or ordinary arm's-length debt interest paid to non-resident corporate beneficial owners; under most DTAs, including the Luxembourg-US DTA, royalty and interest rates are 0%; payments to non-cooperative blacklisted jurisdictions may lose deduction rights under Articles 168/169 LIR and may trigger a punitive deemed-payment treatment; profit-sharing interest exceeding arm's-length terms is treated as a dividend subject to the 15% statutory rate

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A mandatory transfer pricing summary annex is triggered when the aggregate value of intercompany transactions involving the SCSp exceeds EUR 500,000 in a tax year; a full Luxembourg Local File must be prepared and available within 45 days of a direct tax administration request; the OECD-aligned Master File is required where group revenue reaches EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a codified Economic Substance Regulation akin to offshore regimes, but the substance-over-form principle, the Article 56 LIR abus de droit doctrine, the ATAD GAAR, and the OECD minimum standards require the SCSp to demonstrate genuine commercial substance: real office or production premises in Luxembourg, qualified personnel, actual decision-making authority, a Luxembourg bank account, and complete accounting records; a shell-like SCSp with no substance will be recharacterized as a fully taxable Luxembourg entity, lose pass-through treatment, and be denied treaty benefits on all 3D art outsourcing income

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting 3D art outsourcing revenues from Form 700 or partner returns, issuing false invoices to inflate subcontractor costs, using personal PayPal or private foreign bank accounts to receive business income without attribution to the SCSp, or destroying accounting records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; civil re-assessment of all underpaid CIT and MBT plus late-payment interest at 0.8% per month and a 10% surcharge; publication of the conviction; mandatory referral to the Luxembourg Public Prosecutor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners, managers, or directors who knowingly execute the fraud are jointly and severally liable; personal assets may be seized; travel bans and judicial supervision can be imposed during criminal investigation; after final conviction, prohibition from managing any Luxembourg commercial entity for up to 5 years is possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Luxembourg SCSp as a pure invoicing vehicle while the actual 3D sculpting, character rigging, servers, staff, and client negotiations take place outside Luxembourg; appointing a nominee general partner; failing to hold partner meetings or make strategic decisions in Luxembourg; maintaining a mailing address with no real office
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the SCSp as a taxable Luxembourg corporation subject to 24.94% combined CIT/MBT; retroactive taxation of the full profit stream; denial of treaty relief and 15% withholding tax on deemed distributions; loss of pass-through loss deductions; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for failure to deposit accounts; potential de-registration from the RCSL
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is personally and unlimitedly liable for the SCSp's debts including tax liabilities; a bankruptcy action in extension (action en extension de faillite) can be brought against the directors for confusion of assets or fictitious legal arrangements; directors may be ordered to make direct civil restitution to the Luxembourg tax administration and are exposed to travel bans and criminal conviction for fraudulent insolvency
